expected_return.window: scorebord: BUY 13:30 ET on the entry day; SELL amc at the next open, bmo at 13:00 ET on the report day; gross

note: Each member is reported as a percentile of its own live range, 0-100 (pct), with its direction in side; panel_pct (0-100) is the size of the mean of the signed percentiles and side its direction; panel_pct_sd their spread. The selection is panel_pct in the top 20%. panel_score is the signed median of the members' sizes, each read against its own recent history. consensus_k counts members that put the name in their own top 20% on the panel's side; that, not sign agreement, is what selected well on the development names. Certainty (p_up) is recorded and decides nothing. expected_edge_pct is a shrunk in-sample prior, not a forecast. Research only.

opus5.note: The undesignated swap book's direction and per-bp scale are established by the company's own four reported quarters and the 5y rose 90bp in Q3 against a Treasury primary source, so a GAAP headline of roughly $1.55-1.85 on a $1.26 bar (and revenue well above the $38-39m consensus) is close to arithmetic on a newly listed, screener-visible name with four analysts; what holds it down is that the company has itself called the mark non-economic since 2024, a third of it had already given back by 22 October, the unsized AOCI hit from the same move cuts the other way, and the stock sits exactly on the four-analyst $56 target 1.3% off its high with no reaction history at all.

opus55.note: The first listed print likely carries a large unmodelled swap mark-to-market gain from the 90bp Q3 rise in the 5-year yield (i0). That makes a GAAP headline beat, but it is a one-off that management calls non-economic, and a stock already at its targets offsets it (i2). There is no history or options anchor.
